# Runaway and the unregistered distance to the break

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`runaway-distance-unregistered` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F04 · [record](runaway-distance-unregistered.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Every policy through registration, with the rest fixed, that keeps its support leaves any larger unobserved stock unused; before the break, how far off the break is does not register.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. A formation g's policy goes through its registration when, wherever g has registered alike up to a step, its take from and give to every condition it registers are alike in the two flows; the rest is fixed when every other formation's exchange on the conditions g registers is alike at every step; with the same formations present, the two give exchange following registration. (`Becoming.Flow.PolicyThrough`, `Becoming.Flow.OthersFixed`, `Becoming.Flow.ExchangeFollows`, `Becoming.Flow.exchangeFollows_of_policy`)
2. For every policy through registration with the rest fixed, the same formations present and balance at each step on what g registers, the starts differing only in a stock g depends on and does not observe, d higher in the second web: where the first web supports g at every step, the stock stands d higher and g registers alike at every step. (`Becoming.Flow.policy_keeps_difference`, `Becoming.Flow.BalancesOn`, `Becoming.Web.Registers`, `Becoming.Web.RegistersAlike`)
3. Under the same policy, rest, presence and balance, where the second web starts at least as high on what g registers and alike on what g observes, and a difference on a condition g registers has changed by a step, the first web did not support g at every earlier step. (`Becoming.Flow.policy_uses_after_failure`)
4. The web with stock c raised by d at every step, all else as it is, stands at least as high, supports whatever the web supports and stands alike elsewhere; it is dependent where the web is, and a flow balancing on a family balances there on it. (`Becoming.Web.raise`, `Becoming.Web.le_raise`, `Becoming.Web.Supported`, `Becoming.Web.Supported.raise`, `Becoming.Web.raise_other`, `Becoming.Web.Dependent`, `Becoming.Web.Dependent.raise`, `Becoming.Flow.BalancesOn.raise`)
5. At every step at which the web supports g, a raise of a stock g does not observe registers alike for g; observing it, every positive raise registers at every step. (`Becoming.Web.registersAlike_raise`, `Becoming.Web.observed_raise_registers`)
6. Where g does not observe c and c is the only requirement of g that may be unmet up to a horizon u, some raise of c (in the proof, by the sum of the needs up to u) registers alike at every step at which the web supports g and supports g at every step up to u: before the break, how far off it is does not register. (`Becoming.Web.needUpTo`, `Becoming.Web.need_le_needUpTo`, `Becoming.Web.break_not_bounded`)
7. In SupportDrawn the lower web fails the formation at the third step, and a raise registers alike at every step at which the lower web supports it, supports it at the third step and keeps the flow balanced. (`Becoming.SupportDrawn.break_unregistered`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- Balance is assumed only on the conditions registered, at each step (Flow.BalancesOn); the policy going through registration and the rest being fixed are supplied hypotheses, from which exchange following registration is derived; what others respond to is supplied.
- break_not_bounded further assumes that g does not observe c and that c is the only requirement that may be unmet up to the horizon, a local condition.
- Discrete steps, counted from step 0; natural-number levels, needs and amounts; decidable equality of conditions and formations is used only to split cases.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- The laws do not derive that a formation draws more than is renewed, wants to keep its support or forms a policy.
- Loops and gain are not defined, so a runaway remains a reading; what is given here are the two theorems it rests on.
- The raised world uses the same flow, which after the break need not be what the formation would do.
- **Counterexample:** The rest being fixed is needed: where others respond to the stock itself, a higher stock can end the formation first (Attracting.higher_breaks_first), and T5 over policies fails. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Testing.lean)

**Standard boundaries:** Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision. · No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used.

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

Ren's “wisdoms to avoid run away feedbacks”; testing-within-registration read a runaway as a loop running inside a blindness and marked it a heuristic; after experiment-needs-return the AI proposed stating it at the level of policies, and Ren answered “no extra review needed, merge, then continue”. Readings (the AI's, adopted on Ren's delegation): a runaway is a loop whose own registration before the break is that of a world with as much more stock as one likes; its policy cannot use what it does not register; avoiding it without forgoing what is there needs measurement, a model (理) or another formation's registration; this reads Ren's words of 4 October that reason must regulate the heart so that its positive feedback loop does not run out of control.

  - Output: Balance on a family across one step.

- related, not a proved adapter: [reserve-defers-ending](reserve-defers-ending.md). There a reserve defers the end and does not escape it; here how long it defers it does not register.
- related, not a proved adapter: [experiment-needs-return](experiment-needs-return.md). Knowing what one's own act does needs a return and a model of what is irrelevant; here registration through support does not even give the distance to the break.
- related, not a proved adapter: [how-a-carried-difference-grows](how-a-carried-difference-grows.md). Answers the item of its next step asking to define a loop in general and state a runaway as a theorem, for laws of exchange with given coupling strengths: a loop is a chain of couplings of positive strength back to where it started, and what reaches it is multiplied every time around by at least one plus the product of its strengths (carried_runaway); what runs away is the most difference that can arrive, attained by the carrying law. The runaway here is a policy keeping support, and connecting the two stays a next step.
- related, not a proved adapter: [how-loops-form](how-loops-form.md). Here a runaway's break is not registered before it; there the formation of the loop that runs away is not registered by the amounts it carries either: what registers it is what registers the couplings themselves.
- related, not a proved adapter: [loops-within-what-a-law-reads](loops-within-what-a-law-reads.md). Within one law: loops lie within what is read and form where reading grows; for a law reading a stock only below a threshold there is no loop through the stock before the break, and the loop forms at the break.
- related, not a proved adapter: [observation-is-a-route](observation-is-a-route.md). Observation is a route of readings from what is observed: a difference goes only downstream, and a formation registers a stock only through a level it reads downstream of it; a route forms by closing.
